question: Does temperature 0.3 help extreme expert banks under canonical pressure, separating generic router smoothing from the active route-pressure addendum?
hypothesis: If smoothing rather than within-experiment route pressure drives any temperature-0.3 gain, matched canonical-pressure E32/E64 cells will show similar routing reliance and OOD-validation trajectories.
predicted_signature: Temperature-0.3 canonical cells retain nondead expert use and route reliance above 0.01; their paired tail-safe versus no-aux effect and their cross-pressure difference are stable by epochs 30 and 60.
alternative_explanation: Any route-pressure movement is caused by within-experiment balancing or generic optimization noise rather than router smoothing.
falsifier: Canonical cells remain collapsed or differ materially from matched route-pressure cells while the route cells improve, or neither pressure exceeds the locked lower-temperature trajectory.
pruning_rule: At epoch 10, prune a cell dominated on OOD validation, ID retention, worst-experiment accuracy, and its predeclared mechanism signature; allow delayed emergence only through epoch 30. Continue to epoch 60 only if trajectory or route reliance remains competitive.
checkpoint_policy: save epochs 10, 30, and 60 for every arm that reaches the milestone
multiplicity: Exploratory four-cell pressure-control family added before any temperature-0.3 results; all claims remain descriptive until locked fresh-seed confirmation.
